items.title: The dependency-vetting check triggers on workflow action references
body: The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting deterministic trigger keys on package manifests only, so a diff adding googleapis/release-please-action@v5.0.0 — third-party code running with contents:write — showed 'not triggered' and the batch 11 T3 reviewer had to file the missing vetting record by hand.

Fix: extend the trigger — a diff that adds or changes a `uses:` reference under .github/workflows/ requires dependency_vetting with the workflow file in manifests and the action reference in dependencies. Requires the owner's ruling first: the check lives on a STANDING entry (both knowledge copies) and the runner change lives in crates/houserules/src/rules/runner/ (`runner::run` and its report-field module) (batch 20 T3 retired template/tools/kb.mjs, the runner's pre-rewrite home).
Source: batch 11 branch review, violated_rules 2 and template_defects 2 (2026-09-03). Standing-entry change: OWNER RULING PENDING, listed in the batch 11 report.

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): joins batch 35 (2.0.0, batch 3 of 5); the trigger change ships as a security-hygiene pack version through the runner port, and its standing-entry ruling is taken at the batch-35 spec review (D10).
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).

items.title: Curated starter packs: docs style and code quality that adopters add
body: Owner intent (2026-09-04): adopters should start with a curated default set of rules — docs style and code-quality style in tag-pilot's vein — instead of a near-empty seed. Today template/knowledge/ ships 36 entries that are process-heavy (23 process entries) while quality carries 2 and writing-style 3; no docs-style or language-agnostic code-quality starter content exists.

Shape: curate a default entry set for the quality and writing-style topics (and a docs area if warranted), modeled on the tag-pilot checkout's rules as a READ-ONLY reference (houserules.tag-pilot-is-read-only). Content work, independent of the Tier-2 binary; interacts with HR-053 (a starter set is what a modular rules-only install would seed). Curation choices and any new areas go to the batch spec when gated.
Source: owner, 2026-09-04, mid batch 16.

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.147, meta-spec O13): ships after 2.0.0 as a minor, rescoped to curated starter packs (for example docs style and code quality) that the binary carries and a project adds with pack add; the default stays the knowledge-base pack alone (issue 62), and an added pack is a minor change (D2).

items.title: kb audit: an explicit empty-range mode
body: Batch 16 branch review, template defect 2: T5's three empty-range audits (research task, no diff) produced three byte-identical near-vacuous files — every deterministic row passes trivially and none speaks to the actual deliverable; the schema still demands self_audit, so the ritual ran three times for no signal.

Change: give audit an explicit empty-range mode that says so in one summary row (it already emits empty_range: true), and let a research task's report point its evidence rows at the workspace doc instead of the diff. Ships in template/tools until the Tier-2 port owns audit (phase 2), then carries into the Rust audit.
Source: batch 16 branch review retrospective, 2026-09-04.

items.title: check-backlog gains a --fix arm for a non-round-tripping backlog file
body: Filed by the task-1 fix round 1 review (minor issue 8): check-backlog's round-trip finding (HR-076) names a concrete remedy per file class, but only backlog/items/*.json has a shipped command that can reach it (`houserules set`). The other five files (schema.json, amendments.json, batches.json, decisions.json, parked.json) have no writer at all, so an adopter who trips this on one of them is told to hand-reproduce serde_json's pretty-printer byte for byte.

Candidate: a `--fix` arm on check-backlog (or a small subcommand) that rewrites the named file through the same `crate::emit::emit` call the check already compares against, so the repair path and the check path stay the same function. Not built in the fix round that filed it: the message-only remedy was the scoped fix; a --fix arm is a larger surface (does it fix every diverging file in one run, or one named file? does it need a --dry-run?) that deserves its own task.
Owner ruling 2026-10-10 (batch-33 Q1, design.md 5.96): not in 2.0.0. It ships after 2.0.0 as a minor release under the 2.0 surface rule (D2).

items.title: macOS signing and notarization in the dist pipeline
body: Deferred at the batch-25 gate (owner, 2026-09-14; design.md 5.79 discharges 5.37's revisit-at-1.0): 1.0 ships unsigned macOS binaries with the current Gatekeeper bypass documented (run once and let macOS block it, then System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway; amended 2026-09-15, owner ruling - Apple removed right-click-Open in macOS Sequoia). Trigger: real adopter friction with Gatekeeper, not a date. Scope when triggered: the owner's Apple Developer identity and certificates as repository secrets, dist's macos-sign configuration regenerated into release.yml, proven on a watched release.

deferral.reason: 1.0 shipped unsigned macOS binaries

items.title: check-report-claims: HR-110's locative class ('the X live in Y')
body: Batch 25 T3a shipped only HR-110's number class ('N passed', 'N files' next to a cited capture); the locative class the same item names ('a report narrative stating the X live in Y, citing a retained capture, fails when Y is absent from that capture') is not implemented. The two real batch-23 locative instances that motivated HR-110 both sat in a commit body and a plan file, neither a report-narrative field check-report-claims scans, so this task's own corpus run (every retained deliverable in the tracked tree and the batch workspaces) turned up no report-narrative locative instance to derive a mechanical, low-noise trigger from.

Scoped out per quality.gates-derive-their-scope rather than shipped as a guess: a 'the X live in Y' sentence has no citation-adjacent signal as reliable as HR-110's own digit-token match, and this task's corpus run showed even the number class needs real instances to calibrate against (the 'N files (a, b, c)' enumeration-list false positive, fixed in the same task, only surfaced once real corpus data was run through it). Pick this up once a report-narrative locative instance exists to calibrate against, or once a design session derives a trigger some other way; do not ship an untested heuristic against it.

Rider (batch 25 branch review): report_claims.rs is 2889 lines - before this item (or HR-124) lands there, split the three checks and the shared resolver into submodules per the batch-25 plan's god-file direction.
Batch 36 (Task 2) fulfilled the rider: report_claims.rs is split into submodules under crates/houserules/src/report_claims/ (runs.rs, citations.rs, narrative.rs, evidence.rs, natural_red.rs, doc.rs).

items.title: check-report-claims: HR-111's multi-file sweep-coverage case
body: Batch 25 T3a fix round 1: check_narrative_sweep_coverage (HR-111) returns early unless a report's files_changed names exactly one file. Measured over the task's own 350-file corpus (t3a-files-changed-reach.py, retained at .superpowers/sdd/2026-09-14-batch-25/): 3 of 350 deliverables carry exactly one files_changed entry (where the check runs), 93 carry more than one, 3 carry an empty files_changed array, and the remaining 251 are review kinds that carry no files_changed field at all -- so the check is inert on 347 of 350 retained deliverables, the common case by a wide margin.

Blocker: this task's corpus run found no reliable signal for WHICH of several changed files a given sweep/enumeration citation is offered as proof for. Comparing a sweep's content against the WHOLE files_changed list once produced a flood of false positives (a narrowly-scoped sweep has no reason to mention a plan file or a schema copy the same task also edited); a two-citation-per-sentence heuristic (the sweep, then a second citation naming the certified file) would have missed the task's own real motivating instance (HR-111's own origin, batch 23 T1: the sentence names only the sweep, relying on the reader knowing which file the task is about). Picking this up needs either a design session to derive a real per-file attribution signal, or a corpus of real multi-file sweep citations large enough to calibrate one against -- this task's own corpus supplied none.
Origin: batch 25 T3a (HR-111); this item schedules the deferred multi-file case rather than leaving it only as a report concern, per process.no-tech-debt.
Rider (batch 25 branch review): see HR-123's split-first note - the same file hosts both items.
Batch 36 split report_claims.rs; the sweep-coverage check lives in crates/houserules/src/report_claims/citations.rs.

deferral.reason: the multi-file sweep case was left as a report concern

items.title: Vacuousness check for dist-workspace.toml's [dist.github-action-commits] seed table
body: Batch 25 T4 review (reproduced by the reviewer): the seed table is a third exception-shaped list with no vacuousness check - an entry naming an action dist never emits (probe: appending 'actions/never-emitted-by-dist') passes dist-generate-check silently, and the four seeded actions' sha values are by construction of the reseed never compared against anything by that gate (a zeroed 'actions/attest' sha also exits 0). Same class HR-115's vacuous-exception-gate covers for the tree's other two exception-list shapes. Fix: assert every seed-table action appears in dist's generated release.yml (and consider the sha-column direction), in the gate or beside it.

items.title: Deterministic verify-drift warn: a changed verify-listed file flags its entry for re-read
body: Batch 25 branch review: state-only-the-source was the batch's most-violated rule (7 counts + 1 live at the review) - prose describing a mechanism goes stale when a fix round changes the mechanism. Add an audit warn row: when a range changes a file named in an entry's verify list without touching that entry's own topic file, flag the entry ('verify-drift'). Proof case: cite-durable-refs' body described the rejected --base design after 0864f1a changed durable_sha.rs, which its verify names.

items.title: check-report-claims covers reviews; closure-word lint
body: Batch 25 branch review, two arms. (a) Reviews quote counts and outputs like reports do (4 claims-match counts this batch, 3 critical): run check-report-claims over review deliverables and add its clean run to the task-reviewer template's closing act like the implementer template mandates. (b) Closure-word lint: a narrative field containing every/all/no remaining/zero without a named artifact or command in the same field is flagged (4 closure-claim counts this batch; HR-124 books the sweep-coverage widening separately).

items.title: check-knowledge lint: a rule-kind entry without a loading path
body: Batch 25 branch review: an adopted rule landed in an area whose globs no longer covered the files it governs, caught only by judged review. Deterministic floor: flag a rule-kind entry whose standing is false and whose area globs match no tracked file class it names (exact predicate to be designed against areas.json's shape).

items.title: live-run-recipe: a check that requires named command patterns, not just a set field
body: Batch-27 branch review: houserules.live-run-recipe's check (type report-field, field live_run) proves the field is set, not that the recipe's required entries exist - T2 passed every audit while missing the scratch-repo check-knowledge/check-backlog entries the entry's own body requires. Add a check variant that requires named command patterns among a report list-field's entries, or fold the requirement into the summary so a judging reviewer reads it without opening the body.
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).

items.title: vacuous-exception-gate looks for the binary under target/debug and panics under CARGO_TARGET_DIR
body: Found by both implementer scenarios of the batch-28 eval rerun. crates/houserules/src/bin/vacuous-exception-gate.rs builds the path of the houserules binary as `<root>/target/debug/<name>`. With `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` set to a directory outside the repository, the gate panics on the missing path. Both agents worked around it with a temporary `target` symlink.

Scope for the fix: resolve the binary through the build's own target directory (cargo's `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, or the path of the running gate binary), with a named error when the binary is absent. `mise run lint` runs this gate, so the fix needs a test with the variable set.

items.title: No lint covers a script embedded in a workflow
body: Found in batch 28 task 7. `mise run lint` runs shellcheck over the shell files under tools/, template/tools/, and the commit-msg hooks. A `run:` block of a workflow is a shell script too, and no gate reads it: the seeded install step of template/.github/workflows/knowledge.yml (25 lines of bash) and the approve step of .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml are proven only by tests that run them against stubs.

Scope for a spec: extract each `run:` block and pass it to shellcheck in the lint task, or adopt a workflow linter after a dependency vetting. The tests' shared reader (crates/houserules/tests/workflow_reader/) already extracts a step's script.

items.title: Deterministic checks for six judged rules the batch-31 stats run flagged
body: Filed by the batch-31 batch-close loop (process.knowledge-earns-its-place): `houserules stats` over the five most recent workspaces (batches 24 to 30; .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-09-batch-31/stats-t4-batches-24-30.json) proposes `mechanize` without an owner gate for houserules.crash-paths-are-named (2 workspaces), houserules.task-gates-mirror-ci (2), knowledge-base.state-only-the-source (4), process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution (3), quality.user-facing-text-is-contract (2), and writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space (4).

For each entry a spec decides one of two outcomes: a deterministic `check` that catches the class the findings show (task-gates-mirror-ci: compare the report's gate list with .github/workflows and mise.toml; crash-paths-are-named: a lint for unwrap/expect on the named input paths), or the owner tags the entry `ruled-keep` because the rule is judged by design, so the loop stops proposing it.

The batch-32 batch-close run (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-batch-32/stats.json, batches 27 to 32) proposed `mechanize` without an owner gate again for knowledge-base.state-only-the-source, process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution, quality.user-facing-text-is-contract, and writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space; this item covers them, so no new item was filed.
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).

items.title: stats: the budget reason covers a kept set over the budget; two text fixes
body: Deferred at the re-review cap of batch 31 task 1 (process.bounded-review-loop: re-review 2 of 2 on a full-tier task; task-1-review-r2.json in the batch-31 workspace). Reason for deferral: the cap, not a judgment that the findings are wrong.

1 (Important): the `budget` reason always ends 'Demote the others that catch the least.' With every standing entry tagged `ruled-keep` it says so while `candidates` is empty, and with more kept entries than the budget no demotion of the candidates reaches the budget (reproduced in rr2-t1-budget-reason-states.txt). Fix: when `ruled_keep` exceeds the budget, the reason says the kept entries alone exceed it and that lifting a tag is the remedy; tests pin the reason in each state.
2 (Minor): README's sample `narrow` row still prints 'minor or hit a deliverable or prose'; the binary prints 'minor or hit a deliverable'.
3 (Minor): the doc comment of `is_soft` (crates/houserules/src/rules/cost.rs) conditions the prose rule on 'a repository whose docs are its product'; the code applies it everywhere.
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).

deferral.reason: filed at the re-review cap, not a judgment of the findings

items.title: Runner recipes for doc-comment linters and the split of writing-style.doc-comments
body: Source: an adopter's lead-time audit of its batch 3 under houserules 1.2.0 (2026-10-10; design.md 5.94). Issue 6, second half.

writing-style.doc-comments was judged 264 times in this repository's task reviews; the adopter's five doc-comment criticals are what a linter catches (rustdoc missing_docs, ruff D, eslint jsdoc). No check type runs a command, so a lint-backed rule stays a judged row.

Change: a knowledge check type that runs a named project command over the changed files and reads its exit status, plus recipes in the migrating-knowledge skill. A new check type changes the knowledge schema: batch 33, 2.0.0. Continues the mechanize proposals of HR-163.

Owner ruling 2026-10-15 (design.md 5.121, meta-spec M14): ships as the exit-code runner of HR-183's runner port, with migrating-knowledge recipes (rustdoc missing_docs, ruff D, eslint jsdoc). writing-style.doc-comments splits: the id keeps the presence clause (linter-backed, proven); a new judged entry holds the content and naming clauses. Acceptance: the presence rule leaves the judged set; the content rule stays judged.
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).

Conditional (design.md 194): if batch 35 finds that HR-183's runner contract cannot be tested without this exit-code runner, this item joins batch 35 and 2.0.0 with no further ruling; the batch-35 spec records the finding and its probe.

Owner ruling 2026-10-21 (design.md 199(2)): the exit-code parser ships with HR-183 in batch 35. This item keeps only the migrating-knowledge recipes for rustdoc missing_docs, ruff D, and eslint jsdoc, and the split of writing-style.doc-comments into a proven presence rule and a judged content rule (5.121); it stays 2.x.

items.title: check-report-claims flags evidence cited at a session scratchpad or /tmp path
body: From the batch-32 branch review retrospective (.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-batch-32/branch-review.json). process.evidence-outlives-the-session failed twice in batch 32 (task 2 round 0: a docs_verified source with no capture; the ledger: a scratchpad path).

Change: a report `source`, `output`, or evidence string that names a path under the session scratchpad or /tmp is a claim mismatch unless a workspace capture is cited beside it. A knowledge check cannot read report strings today; the checker can (crates/houserules/src/report_claims/narrative.rs, check_ephemeral_paths; batch 36 spec 6 check 7 now walks every report string for a /tmp or scratchpad path).
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).

items.title: cargo-deny prints five duplicate-version warnings on every lint run
body: Found in the batch-30 task review. deny.toml sets `multiple-versions = "warn"` under `[bans]`, and `mise run lint` therefore prints five `warning[duplicate]` blocks on every run (measured 2026-10-02: base64, getrandom, syn, windows-link, windows-sys, two versions each, all transitive). A gate that always prints warnings trains readers to skip its output: a task report of batch 30 called the lint output clean. Scope for a ruling: keep the level and say so in deny.toml with the reason; or list the five as `skip` entries so that a new duplicate stands out; or set the level to `deny` after the list exists.

items.title: Propose rules from escaped defects (issue 69)
body: Issue 69 asks for houserules learn <commit> for a revert or a fix commit with a trailer such as Fixes-Escape: <sha>: it traces the original change to its audit report and proposes a new or tighter rule as a draft knowledge entry with the escape as source; stats counts escapes per rule and per area. Acceptance: for a revert of an audited commit, learn names the uncovered hunk or the passed rule the defect slipped through; the draft passes check-knowledge.
The owner scheduled it for 2.0.0 on 2026-10-15: every open GitHub issue ships in 2.0.0 (design.md 5.98). Close issue 69 on the 2.0.0 release.
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).

items.title: Link specs and agent sessions into the audit (issue 70)
body: Issue 70 asks that audit and evidence read optional commit trailers and PR links for a spec reference (Spec Kit, OpenSpec, or a plan file) and an agent session reference (for example Entire-Checkpoint), show them in the evidence packet, and offer two optional rules: changes in configured areas reference a spec, and a referenced spec file exists. Acceptance: trailers are optional unless a rule requires them; houserules has no dependency on any spec or session tool.
The owner scheduled it for 2.0.0 on 2026-10-15: every open GitHub issue ships in 2.0.0 (design.md 5.98). Close issue 70 on the 2.0.0 release.
Back in 2.0.0 by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 193).

items.title: Route every rule and configuration change to human review (issue 73)
body: Issue 73 asks for protected paths (knowledge/, .houserules.json, the schemas, area globs, tier thresholds, check-runner configuration, the seeded CI workflow, .githooks/, the diff-size budgets and PR template of issue 58, plus project paths): a change that touches one gets the highest tier and is never auto-merge-eligible; audit and the tier decision use the rules at the merge base; a rule change is also audited against the new rules, with both results and a plain-language rule diff; the change record stores the merge-base rules hash. Acceptance: a branch that lowers a threshold and adds code the old threshold rejects fails audit; a branch that only edits knowledge/ gets the highest tier; the record of a rule change shows the old and new rules hash.
The owner scheduled it for 2.0.0 on 2026-10-15: every open GitHub issue ships in 2.0.0 (design.md 5.98). Close issue 73 on the 2.0.0 release.

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.126, meta-spec review F6): the merge-base rules are read from git at the merge base (knowledge/, the copied packs, .houserules.json) with their checksums checked, with no network and no old binary.

Owner ruling 2026-10-16 (design.md 5.151, meta-spec O17), delivered with this item: when the merge base has no install schema, audit reads its rules through the 1.x conversion in memory (no write, no network, no old binary) and prints one line saying so; D4 applies to HEAD only; the upgrade pull request is audited against the converted merge-base rules and HEAD's rules, both results reported, and gets the highest tier; the batch-37 live run shows this for an install from each released tag.

Owner ruling 2026-10-19 (design.md 5.153, meta-spec O19), delivered with this item: the in-memory 1.x conversion of the merge base maps the layout only (packs, local pack, overrides, exclusions, the area model), reads every entry's text from the merge base, and pins nothing to the binary's packs; the merge-base audit applies the 1.x rules as written, and the HEAD audit the 2.0 rules.
Moved out of 2.0.0 to a 2.x minor release by the owner's ruling of 2026-10-21 (design.md 192).
Ruled 2026-10-25 (design.md 271): the upgrade proof against converted 1.x merge-base rules (meta-spec 7, 5.151(4)) runs with this item, not in batch 38.

items.title: pack add takes an HTTPS source for an upstream pack
body: Owner ruling 2026-10-19 (design.md 5.164): batch 33 ships pack add from a git source (git+<url>@<tag>#<path>, through the user's git) and from a local file; an HTTPS source is this backlog item, not scheduled.

Scope: pack add https://.../pack.json fetches one pack file and pins it by source and content checksum, like the other sources. It needs an HTTP client library (the binary has none for packs; axoupdater serves only the self-update) and a way to pass a token for a private host. Every gate keeps reading only the copies in the tree (5.126).

items.title: Nested houserules installs in one repository
body: Batch-33 spec controller call C12 (2026-10-19), under design.md 5.168: batch 33 lets one repository hold several installs but has init refuse an install root inside another install's root, or one that holds another install. A nested pair would make one change belong to two installs' gates (audit, check-commit, the CI paths filters), and no ruling says which install's rules apply. The owner checks C12 at the batch-33 spec gate.

Scope: a rule for which install owns a path inside a nested root (for example, the outer install's gates skip paths under an inner root), applied to for, audit, check-commit, and the seeded workflows' paths filters; init then accepts a nested root.

items.title: Deterministic checks for four judged rules that keep failing
body: Batch-33 close (stats.json over batches 28 and 30-33, proposals with owner_gate false): mechanize houserules.crash-paths-are-named (2 workspaces), knowledge-base.state-only-the-source (5), quality.user-facing-text-is-contract (4), and writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space (4). Each failed or drew a finding in that many workspaces as a judged rule.

Scope: for each rule, a deterministic audit check where one is sound (for example a user-facing line of the binary that no test pins whole, or a printed example that a gate then rejects), or a recorded reason why the rule stays judged.

items.title: Batch-33 template and gate defects from the branch review
body: Batch-33 branch review, retrospective template_defects, and the live run:
1. audit --workspace and stats skip a task-*-report.json whose task id does not match \d+[a-z]? (task-3-4-integration-report.json) with no line; they should list or refuse it by name.
2. The report-field evidence counts the reports that triggered the check, not the reports read; print both counts.
3. The orchestrating skill never removes an implementer's worktree or its worktree-agent-* branch after integration; 23 were left, and Claude Code loaded their template skills as duplicates.
4. A spec's upgrade acceptance case should list the adopter-side reds a kit change causes by design (the process.evals-rerun red of live case 17).

5. vacuous-exception-gate panics when CARGO_TARGET_DIR points outside the checkout and target/debug/residue-gate is absent (live case 19); it should build or locate the binary, or name the missing path in one line.

items.title: check-report-claims: a cited stats run names the file that holds its window
body: Deferred from batch 34 (spec revision 4, round-3 design review T25): HR-165 point 3's second half. The rule needs a detection pattern for a cited stats run, and houserules.plan-semantics-run-on-the-corpus requires that pattern to run over the real corpus before a plan fixes it. Batch 34 ships the first half (a cited workspace path must exist).

Scope: define how check-report-claims recognizes a cited stats run in a report, a spec, or a backlog item; run the pattern over the deliverables of batches 28 to 34; give the finding line; check that the cited run names its stats-batches-<a>-<b>.json window file.
Batch 36 split report_claims.rs; the workspace-path check of documents lives in crates/houserules/src/report_claims/doc.rs.

deferral.reason: the detection rule needs a corpus run before a plan fixes it

items.title: pack upgrade and pack remove: an optIn id that a new version keeps but no longer lists
body: Deferred from batch 34 (Task 4 fix round 1, concerns 2 and 3). A pack version that keeps an entry but drops its id from optIn leaves the opt-in exclusion in place, and pack remove then refuses with the exclusion line. The untaken offer is houserules' own data, as it is for a dropped entry, so upgrade should withdraw it. Separately, a pack remove that stops after it withdraws an offer and before it removes the copy leaves the entry live until the rerun finishes the removal.

Reason for the deferral: in 2.0 no kit pack lists optIn but the process pack, whose one optIn id ships in batch 34, so no released version can drop it yet. Scope: withdraw an untaken offer whose id leaves optIn on upgrade; order pack remove so that no stop leaves an untaken opt-in entry live; a locked-file stop test for each.

deferral.reason: no released kit pack can drop an optIn id in 2.0; only the process pack lists one

items.title: dependency-vetting: trigger on mise tool files
body: Found by the batch 34 Task 3 review. The security-hygiene.dependency-vetting check's if globs list package, Cargo, Python, Go, Ruby, and PHP manifests, but not mise.toml, .mise.toml, mise.*.toml, or .tool-versions, so a change that adds a tool through mise passes the row without vetting.

Scope: the check's if globs cover every project config file that mise reads, at any depth (mise docs, configuration.md 'Config file locations'): **/mise.toml, **/.mise.toml, **/mise.*.toml, **/.tool-versions, **/mise/config.toml, **/mise/conf.d/**/*.toml, **/.mise/config.toml, **/.mise/conf.d/**/*.toml, **/.config/mise.toml, **/.config/mise/*.toml, **/.config/mise/conf.d/**/*.toml; with a regression test per location (an audit of a commit that adds a mise tool without dependency_vetting fails the row). The Task 9 review widened the first four-glob scope. Delivered by batch 34 Task 9.

items.title: Compatibility with OpenSpec in 2.0.0
body: Owner, 2026-10-21, verbatim: "I just caught a gap in the meta-spec: we need to be compatible in some way with openspec and github spec kit (openspec has preference)."

Research so far (controller, 2026-10-21, against the current docs: OpenSpec v1.14.3, docs/agent-contract.md, docs/customization.md, docs/supported-tools.md; Spec Kit v1.2.2, docs/reference/agentic-sdd.md, docs/reference/extensions.md): OpenSpec keeps specs and changes under openspec/ (changes/<id>/proposal.md, design.md, tasks.md, delta specs; archive/), has a JSON agent contract (list, show, status, validate, archive --json), and takes project context, per-artifact rules, and apply/archive guidance from openspec/config.yaml. Spec Kit keeps .specify/ and per-feature spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, and has an extension system with before_<command> and after_<command> hooks registered in .specify/extensions.yml.

Open: the owner rules what compatible means (coexistence, the houserules step inside their implement phase, their changes as work items, houserules rules rendered into their context), the release it lands in, and whether it supersedes design.md 184(2) (no recipe for another workflow ships).
Ruled 2026-10-21 (design.md 191): OpenSpec support ships in 2.0.0; Spec Kit moves to HR-210, a minor release after 2.0.0.

The adapter of this item settles which sections it reads from the OpenSpec version it pins, and amends that table.

Ruled 2026-10-25 (design.md 266): an `openspec` intent adapter and an `openspec validate --json` file input for evidence, record, and bundle check, plus a documented openspec/config.yaml hookup in the README and docs; houserules never edits that file; 184(2) is superseded for that hookup only.

items.title: Rewrite README for 2.0.0: when and why houserules fits, the consistency layer, and its clean integration
body: Owner, 2026-10-21, verbatim: "Make sure that you rewrite the readme when we publish v2. Users must know at a glance when and why houserules is the right solution for them and they must know that houserules can be the central layer that keeps their ai-native coding consistent instead of diverging into whatever agents deem correct in the moment with their limited knowledge of a session. Adhere to the best-practices of README writing that you have once researched and make sure to research beforehand, what makes houserules unique and strong against other solutions and make those advantages clear."
Owner, 2026-10-21, verbatim: "Also make clear that it integrates cleanly with the other solutions (which in and of itself is a big strength of houserules v2)."

Scope: (1) Research first, at spec time, with sources recorded in the batch workspace: current README practice (re-checked against the batch-26 research of design.md 84 and writing-style.readme-is-an-adopter-funnel), and what makes houserules unique and strong against the other solutions that adopters weigh (for example per-harness rule files such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor rules, and Copilot instructions; rule-sync tools; spec-driven toolkits such as OpenSpec and Spec Kit; agent memory banks); each claimed advantage is verified against the tree and the sources, never assumed. (2) The README's first screen says when and why houserules is the right solution, and that it can be the central layer that keeps AI-native coding consistent across agents, harnesses, and sessions, instead of each agent deciding in the moment from a session's limited knowledge. (3) The rest follows the adopter funnel: value, install, runnable usage, then depth; no process history, no claims that rot with releases. (4) The README makes clear that houserules integrates cleanly with those other solutions, a strength of 2.0 in its own right: it renders into the harnesses' own rule files, reads work items through the adopter's tracker, and works under OpenSpec and other workflows; each integration claim is shown by a run, not asserted. (5) The owner reviews the rewrite before the release is cut.

items.title: Refuse an empty defaultBranch in the install marker
body: Batch-37 T12 fix-diff review (task-12-review-r1.json, out_of_scope[0]): `Marker::validate` accepts any string as `defaultBranch`, the empty string included. `durable-sha` refuses an empty name as naming no branch, while the GitHub forms of `ci print` and `ci write` print `branches: [""]` with exit 0, a trigger that never fires. body: Batch-37 stats.json (batches 33 to 37) and branch-review.json propose deterministic checks for judged rules that failed or drew findings in two or more workspaces: houserules.platform-gated-tests (a lint test that fails a #[cfg(unix)], #[cfg(windows)], or #[cfg(target_os line whose previous non-blank line is no comment); houserules.task-gates-mirror-ci (a report-facts `gates` field listing the gate commands in `tests`, with a report-field check); process.report-evidence-verbatim and process.claims-match-artifacts (check-report-claims extended to the file:line references of self_review and concerns); process.wiring-checks-run-the-resolution; quality.absence-is-designed (a lint test that fails an Option printed with {:?} in a user-facing line); quality.lint-the-token-not-the-document; process.evidence-outlives-the-session (a check that fails a report citing a session scratchpad path); process.closure-claims-carry-enumeration (a report-field text check for every/all/no remaining without a capture); writing-style.doc-comments (RUSTDOCFLAGS=-Dwarnings cargo doc --no-deps in mise run lint); and houserules.pinned-git-text-runs-hermetic (a grep-absent warn for a git grep -l without --no-color).

The narrow rows of stats (task-gates-mirror-ci, deliverables-json, absence-is-designed: narrow to contract surfaces) are decided with the mechanize rows of the same ids: a deterministic check narrows the judged rule by itself (branch-review recommendation).

Deferred: each check is a code change of its own with its paper walk (process.gates-cover-generated-commits); batch 37 closes on its own scope. The git grep pattern hits two #[cfg(test)] calls of review/git.rs that parse no names, so that check needs a test-code exclusion first.

items.title: Fix two implementer-template defects that batch 37's branch review names
body: Branch-review.json template_defects 3 and 4: the implementer template asks every fix round for a mutation row on each added test that passes before the fix, while the task-reviewer template's step 9 lifts the row for a critical task; and the implementer template's refusal line lacks the sentence of process.refused-commands-hand-back's body that names a shell glob or a variable as another way (the dependency-add eval implementer redid two refused commands, .claude/evals/record.json).
Fix: add to the fix-round paragraph that the row is optional for a critical task, and copy the refusal sentence into the template's refusal line; run every eval scenario (process.evals-rerun).
Deferred: a change of the implementer template needs an eval run, and batch 37's run closed at its controller step 5; the batch that next changes a template or a scenario takes it.

deferral.reason: Deferred: a change of the implementer template needs an eval run, and batch 37's run closed at its controller step 5; the batch that next changes a template or a scenario takes it.

items.title: Ship batch 37's retrospective additions to kit pack entries
body: The batch-37 knowledge commit added one body sentence each to knowledge-base.state-only-the-source, quality.gates-derive-their-scope, and writing-style.instructions-cover-the-state-space through knowledge/overrides.json, so this repository reads them while the kit packs do not ship them.
Fix: move each sentence into its pack under template/packs/, move the pack versions by class through KIT_PACK_VERSIONS and the checksum tests, run update --dir ., and drop the three body overrides.
Deferred: a pack content change is a kit change with its own version moves and tests, beyond a knowledge commit at batch close.

items.title: Give the process area a loading path for its controller rules
body: Batch-37 branch review recommendation: knowledge/areas.json gives the `process` area no globs, so no process-pack rule reaches an audit unless it is standing, and the controller-tagged entries of that area are judged by no audit row.

Fix: give the area the globs of the files its rules govern (docs/specs/**, docs/plans/**, the workspaces folder), or state in knowledge-base.controller-rules-are-tagged that the branch review judges the process-area controller rules from the ledger; walk the audit packages of a task and of a branch before and after.
Deferred: it changes which rules every audit package holds, a change with its own walk, beyond the batch-37 close.
